Bethany — thanks, this is very clear. Quick summary and a pragmatic checklist to move to an integration runbook.

SAML attributes (minimal required):
- NameID (email) -> primary user identifier
- "groups" -> used for coarse role assignment (RBAC)
- "roles" (optional) -> direct role assertion we can map to control-plane roles
- "department" -> optional for tenant-scoping policies
- "email_verified" -> boolean for account activation gating

Implementation notes: Redwood private control plane supports both attribute-based mapping and SCIM reconciliation; if you assert "roles" we can do one-to-one role binds without SCIM. If you rely on groups, SCIM should be enabled for stable lifecycle (deprovisioning).

SCIM behavior:
- We accept RFC7644-compliant SCIM payloads.
- Nested groups: we treat nested groups as separate group objects; our mapping UI lets you define transitive expansion rules (e.g., includeChildren=true). If Okta sends only parent groups, send explicit membership or we will need a sync job on your side to flatten.

Service account pattern:
- Recommended: OIDC + client credentials (JWT assertion) from your IdP to Redwood's private token exchange endpoint (mutual TLS optional).
- We also support short-lived service tokens via SAML 2.0 Bearer assertion for customers with legacy flows.

Attachments: see the quick checklist I attached (privcp-iam-checklist.pdf) for required metadata and cert formats.

Next steps: can your Okta admin share an example SAML assertion and a SCIM group listing (JSON export)? If yes, Mina & Marcus will run a dry-mapping in our test tenant and return a mapping proposal.

—Jonas

Adding more technical detail and an Excel schematic (saml-attribute-map.xlsx) — attached. Highlights from our internal runbook: 

1) Role-binding precedence
- Explicit SAML "roles" claim wins over SCIM group-provisioned roles.
- If both present, we log a precedence event and tag the user for manual review during the initial roll (first 24h).

2) SCIM sync cadence and conflict handling
- Recommended cadence: 5–15 minutes for active user pools, 1h for large orgs (>50k users).
- Conflict policy: remote (IdP) is source-of-truth; Redwood client will apply patches unless a protected service account is affected.

3) Service accounts / agent access
- We recommend creating a dedicated SCIM user (type=service) with a corresponding role-binding that has a ManagedServiceAccount tag.
- Preferred flow: OIDC client credentials grant -> audience-limited JWT -> call to /v1/private/token-exchange -> short-lived PrivCP token (1h default).
- Mutual TLS: supported for FIPS/Zoned deployments; we can require mTLS for token-exchange endpoint if requested.

4) Audit & cert rotation
- Audit logs for auth events are written to S3-compatible buckets in your VPC (we ship a CloudTrail-style schema).
- Cert rotation: we require active cert rollover every 90 days for IdP signing certs used in SAML. We provide a cert-roll webhook to notify your ops team 14d before expiry.

Attached files: saml-attribute-map.xlsx (attribute->role mapping examples)

I will schedule a short tech call with Acme's Okta admin and Marcus to validate a sample SAML assertion.

Mina
